name: Flocking
miniText: How can coordinated motion arise without a leader? NetLogo Flocking applies separation, alignment, and cohesion using locally visible neighbors. These rules correspond to the distributed flocking tradition introduced by Reynolds [1], while minimal alignment models [2] and empirical work on neighbor selection [3] clarify which assumptions matter. The simulation illustrates moving groups that form and reorganize through repeated local updates. Its bounded turns, chosen vision distance, and stylized motion do not explicitly model flight energetics, sensory uncertainty, or aerodynamic interactions. A coherent flock demonstrates an emergent property of these rules. It does not establish that a particular bird species uses the same metric neighborhood or that every parameter setting maintains cohesion.
